chunks: And ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh and a group (of scholars) narrated to me, may Allah have mercy on them, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Amir, from Jabir al-Makfuf, from Abi al-Samit, who said:

I heard Abu ‘Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on foot, Allah will record for him one thousand good deeds for every step, erase one thousand bad deeds for him, and raise his status by one thousand degrees.
So when you arrive at the Euphrates, perform ritual bath (ghusl), hang your shoes, and walk barefoot, walking with the gait of a humble slave.

So when you arrive at the door of al-Ha’ir, recite Takbir four times, then walk a little, then recite Takbir four times, then approach his head and stand upon it, then recite Takbir four times [recite Takbir and pray near him and ask], and pray four units (rak’ahs) and ask Allah for your need.

key_terms.بَابُ الْحَائِر: The door of the enclosure (referring to the shrine area)
key_terms.قَبْرُ الْحُسَيْنِ (ع): The grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards and ritual steps for visiting Imam Husayn's grave on foot according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* emphasizes the merit of pilgrimage on foot, reflecting the Shia tradition of physical humility and bodily devotion in visiting the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). It details specific ritual etiquette, such as bathing at the Euphrates and walking barefoot, which symbolize the transition from the mundane to the sacred space of the 'Hir' (enclosure). The promise of a thousand good deeds per step underscores the concept of *ziyarat* as an act of worship that elevates the believer's spiritual rank and erases sins.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 4. ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain ibn Mūsā ibn Bābawayh and a group (of my scholars) narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Mughīrah, from ‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir, from Jābir Al-Makfūf, from Abil Sāmit, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: Allāh will register one thousand good deeds and erase one thousand bad deeds for every step taken by those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) on foot. He will also increase their status one thousand times (for every step taken).
Imam (a.s.) added: When you arrive at the Euphrates (River), perform Ghusl, carry your shoes, and walk barefoot like a humble slave.

Once you arrive at the door of the Ḥā`ir, recite (the phrase of) TAKBǏR four times. Then walk a little and repeat this four more times. Then approach the location close to his head, stand there and repeat it four more times. Establish prayers next to his grave and ask Allāh for your needs.
